config.aronalayersgen.open_folder.toolti: Open config/aronalayersgen, which also holds the block mapping files
config.aronalayersgen.option.layer_injec: Master switch for layer generation. Where each dimension's layer heights come from is detected from its own world generator: Tellus worlds use Tellus elevation data, FreeTerraForged and ReTerraForged dimensions use their terrain cells, any other noise-based world (vanilla, amplified, datapack terrain, and the Nether and End of TerraForged or Tellus worlds) uses the sub-block surface recovered from vanilla's density field, and flat, void and other generators get no layers. The log names each dimension's source the first time it generates ([Layers] ...).
config.aronalayersgen.option.injection_m: When to inject layers: CARVERS (before structures, may need cleanup) or POST_FEATURES (after structures, cleaner result).
config.aronalayersgen.option.3D_layer_in: Experimental, needs VanillaLayer+ 5.0.0 or later. On TerraForged terrain (FreeTerraForged / ReTerraForged), a floor layer with a higher terrain block beside it becomes a 3D layer (<name>_3d_layer): the same floor height merged with a wall toward the step, its thickness measured from the surfaces on either side. Open cells up a step also get a 3D layer of the wall's material with no floor part (vertical_layers 0), so only hard faces (stone-like and ores) get one. Floor layers on flat ground stay normal layers. Uses vp_block_mappings.json, even when Conquest Reforged is also installed.
config.aronalayersgen.option.tellus_redu: Reduce the Tellus layer count by one (round(depth*8)-1). Legacy RTF aesthetic tweak; leaving it false makes layers track true sub-block elevation and avoids ~19% of columns dropping to zero on near-integer elevations. Snow columns always use the un-reduced value regardless. Only affects the Tellus backend.
config.aronalayersgen.option.fractional_: Reduce the fractional-surface layer count by one (round(fraction*8)-1), as the RTF path does. True keeps the established look: the shallowest columns stay bare (fraction < 3/16, about 19% of them) and the rendered surface sits a constant ~0.875 above the true one. False layers every column with any fill at all, giving thicker layers and a clean 1.0 offset, at the cost of almost no bare ground. A layer is capped so it never fills its whole block either way, so turning this off does not bring block-height layers back. Only affects the fractional-surface backend.

Smallest vertical density change per block at which the reconstructed surface position is trusted. The reconstruction carries a small absolute error (~0.02); where density falls steeply through the surface (beaches, plains, ordinary slopes) that error is negligible, but on high peaks the field flattens out and the same error moves the crossing a whole block, which reported 251 of 256 columns as full and buried the peak under a uniform slab. Columns below this are left to vanilla instead. Only consulted where the field and the placed world already disagree, so it cannot remove layers from terrain that produces a valid crossing. Raise it if peaks still get slabbed, lower it if ordinary terrain loses layers; watch flatGradient in the debug output. Measured snowy_slopes chunks put ALL 256 columns under 0.01 while still producing clean crossings and smooth gradients, so the once-suggested 0.03 would strip a whole chunk that works. Enable only with debug output in front of you.

Fraction of a chunk's columns that may disagree with the density field before the whole chunk is left to vanilla. 1.0 never skips. Measured rates: beach 0%, plains 23-42%, jagged peaks 61% -- so this separates peaks from ordinary ground by only about eight points, and an earlier default of 0.25 cut through normal plains and stripped their layers. 0.5 is a judgement call rather than a boundary the data draws: it clears every plains chunk measured and still skips peaks, but a plains chunk above 50% would lose its layers. Raise toward 1.0 if layers go missing on ordinary terrain; the cost is peaks getting a uniform full-thickness slab instead of vanilla ground. Watch the disagreement line in /algdebug.

Interpolate each of the router's Interpolated markers separately, the way vanilla's NoiseChunk does, instead of interpolating the whole density tree as one unit. A measured world has five such markers, so vanilla interpolates five separate sub-expressions and evaluates everything combining them per block; where those operations are nonlinear (clamps, squeeze, multiplication, slides) the two are different functions. Whole-tree interpolation agrees closely on gentle terrain but placed the surface 1-3 blocks above the world on jagged peaks, which is what forced the overfull, block-mismatch and min-gradient guards to exist. Costs a tree rebuild per chunk.
config.aronalayersgen.option.skip_snowy_: Skip layer generation in snowy/cold biomes to avoid interfering with natural snow.
config.aronalayersgen.option.improve_sno: Use vanilla snow layers in snowy biomes with original un-reduced layer value. Plant conversion, rocks, foliage still apply.
config.aronalayersgen.option.break_snow_: When breaking a snow layer, replace it with the mapped layer block (from block_mappings) based on the block below, with layer value reduced by 1.
config.aronalayersgen.option.underwater_: Enable layer placement on underwater surfaces (ocean/river floors). Layer blocks must support waterlogging.
config.aronalayersgen.option.replace_dir: When placing layers on dirt_path, also replace the dirt_path block with the full-block equivalent of the layer (e.g. conquest:sandy_soil).
config.aronalayersgen.option.place_wet_s: When placing a sand layer (conquest:sand_layer), use conquest:wet_sand_layer instead if the layer will be waterlogged or is below Y=63 (sea level).
config.aronalayersgen.option.reduce_swam: Lower the layer count in swamp biomes (any biome whose id contains 'swamp': swamp, mangrove swamp, and modded swamps) by reduce_swamp_layers_value; a count reduced to 0 places no layer. Swamp ground sits around the water line, and full-height layers there stand proud of the water.
How many layers (eighths of a block) to remove in swamp biomes when reduce_swamp_layers is on.
config.aronalayersgen.option.swamp_puddl: Leave swamp puddles as water. Vanilla's swamp surface rule turns the top block at Y=62 into one-block water puddles while the density field still describes ground there; with this on those columns get no layer and stay vanilla water (lily pads untouched), off they receive a near-full waterlogged layer.
config.aronalayersgen.option.plant_injec: Enable plant injection: layer blocks become transparent to plant placement, and vanilla plants above layers are converted to Conquest variants.
config.aronalayersgen.option.replace_sea: Convert vanilla seagrass/tall_seagrass to Conquest equivalents. Conquest seagrass lacks the layer property, so they are placed without a layer value.
config.aronalayersgen.option.tree_inject: Enable tree injection: layer blocks become transparent to tree feature generation, allowing trees to grow on layered terrain.
config.aronalayersgen.option.trees_on_la: Trees, huge mushrooms and chorus plants stand on top of the layer instead of inside it: generated ones start one block higher with the layer placed under them, saplings and mushrooms grow on top of the layer, and their trunk or stem is drawn down to the layer (outline and collision follow). Breaking the base no longer leaves a hole. false = the soil layer under a tree becomes dirt and chorus columns are left unlayered. Install on client and server alike.
config.aronalayersgen.option.posts_on_la: Fences, walls, glass panes and iron bars placed on a layer are drawn down to it (the post and wall sides reach the ground, rails stay where they are), and their outline and the collision of the layer under them follow, so animals cannot slip under a fence built on low layers. Fence gates are left as they are. Install on client and server alike.

EXTEND: the post is drawn down to the layer, its top stays level with its neighbours, and a wall one level lower is joined across the step. LOWER: the whole post is lowered onto the layer like a brewing stand, so it follows the ground; where it meets a post at another height the end of the side is closed instead of showing its inside.
config.aronalayersgen.option.lowered_pos: A lowered fence or wall reaches back up to a block standing on it (a slab, a lantern), closing the gap lowering opens under that block. Only the parts that reached the top of the post (a fence's post, a wall's post and tall sides) are stretched. false = the gap stays.
config.aronalayersgen.option.cr_nbt_tree: Place hand-crafted CR trees from NBT files during world generation. Tree species and biomes are configured in cr_nbt_trees.json. NBT files live in nbt_trees/<species>/.
When cr_nbt_trees=true and no NBT species is found for a growing sapling (not configured or no files), allow vanilla tree generation to proceed. false = suppress vanilla, sapling will not grow.
config.aronalayersgen.option.plant_groun: Lower plants standing on a partial-height layer block so they sit on its surface instead of floating at the top of the block. Works at runtime for every plant, generated or placed by hand. Plants are detected automatically: vanilla plant classes (flowers, grass, saplings, mushrooms, seagrass...), column plants (sugar cane, bamboo, cactus, kelp) and any block with a random ground offset and no collision; blocks that already position themselves on layers (a 'layers'/'layer'/'offset_toggle' property, e.g. Conquest Reforged plants) and hanging states are skipped. Install on client and server alike.
Also lower the selection outline and collision box of grounded plants, so they are targeted where they are drawn. false = visual offset only.
config.aronalayersgen.option.ground_deco: Also lower free-standing decorations onto the layer: lanterns, floor torches, candles and candle cakes, flower pots, carpets, pressure plates, brewing stands and cakes. Their flame and smoke particles move down with them. Blocks drawn by a block-entity renderer (chests, signs, skulls, banners, beds) are not lowered.
config.aronalayersgen.option.plant_groun: Block ids to ground even though automatic detection rejects them.
Block ids never to ground, even though automatic detection accepts them.
config.aronalayersgen.option.place_rocks: Place rock blocks above layers on mapped surface blocks. Uses cr_rock_mappings.json for surface-to-rock mapping.
config.aronalayersgen.option.conquest_en: Per-biome weighted rock placement using cr_enhanced_rock_mappings.json. Uses chance_to_place_rocks unless overridden per biome. Biomes not in the file fall back to cr_rock_mappings.json.
config.aronalayersgen.option.chance_to_p: Chance (0.0-1.0) to place a rock above an eligible layer. 0.1 = 10% chance. Recommended: 0.05-0.2.
config.aronalayersgen.option.rock_densit: How rock density (1-4) is chosen: RANDOM (uniform) or DECREASED (biased toward smaller rocks, controlled by rock_density_factor).
Bias strength for DECREASED mode. Each density has 1/factor the chance of the previous. 1.0 = uniform, 4.0 = ~75/19/5/1% distribution. Recommended: 3.0-5.0.
config.aronalayersgen.option.place_extra: Place conquest foliage above layers on mapped surface blocks where the position is empty. Uses cr_extra_foliage_mappings.json.
config.aronalayersgen.option.conquest_en: Per-biome weighted grass placement using cr_enhanced_extra_foliage.json. Uses chance_to_place_extra_foliage.
config.aronalayersgen.option.chance_to_p: Chance (0.0-1.0) to place extra foliage above an eligible layer. 0.1 = 10% chance. Recommended: 0.05-0.3.
config.aronalayersgen.option.structure_i: Enable structure-aware layer injection: layers are not placed inside structure piece bounding boxes (buildings, roads, etc.). Required by all structure sub-features below.
config.aronalayersgen.option.cross_chunk: Also check structure references in neighboring chunks to catch structures that start outside the current chunk. May cause server tick timeouts during heavy pre-generation (e.g. Chunky). Disable when pre-generating.
config.aronalayersgen.option.structure_f: Suppress layers within the overall XZ footprint of each StructureStart (the hull of all its pieces). Catches cleared ground, plazas and paths between buildings that fall between individual piece bounding boxes. Trees are not affected (they have no StructureStart).
How many blocks below the structure start's minimum Y to still suppress layers. Handles terrain carved into by the structure (paths dug into a hillside, excavated basements).

How many blocks above the structure start's maximum Y to still suppress layers. RTF terrain within a footprint can sit a few blocks above the highest roof piece; without this margin those surface columns escape detection. Keep small to avoid suppressing layers legitimately above underground structures (e.g. mineshaft at Y=50, surface at Y=65 — with default 4 the gap is 15 so surface is not suppressed).
config.aronalayersgen.option.structure_i: Expand each structure piece bounding box outward in XZ by structure_injection_extra_bounds_distance blocks, adding a buffer zone where layers are also suppressed.
Radius (blocks) to expand structure bounding boxes outward in XZ when structure_injection_extra_bounds=true.
config.aronalayersgen.option.enclosed_sp: Skip layers if there is a solid block (ceiling) within enclosed_space_height blocks above the layer position. Catches enclosed interiors not covered by bounding boxes.
Maximum height (blocks) to scan above a layer position when looking for a ceiling. Recommended: 4-6.
config.aronalayersgen.option.structure_c: Post-injection correction pass: remove layers where a solid ceiling is detected above or the surface block is a known structure material.
config.aronalayersgen.option.structure_n: Heightmap-based detection: captures the pre-feature heightmap and removes layers where structures raised the terrain by 2+ blocks.
config.aronalayersgen.option.second_pass: After structure_injection or structure_no_layers removes/blocks a layer, taper the 8 in-chunk neighbors: cap values above 4 to 4, decrement others by 1, remove at 0.
config.aronalayersgen.option.conservativ: At injection time, compare the current surface Y against RTF's noise-derived base Y. If it deviates beyond the up/down tolerances, skip the layer. Catches any structure that raises or lowers the terrain at a column, regardless of shape or type.
Maximum upward deviation (blocks) between actual surface Y and RTF's expected base Y. 1 tolerates natural snow (+1 block) while still catching structures that raised terrain by 2+.

Maximum downward deviation (blocks) between actual surface Y and RTF's expected base Y. 0 is strict (natural terrain sits exactly at RTF's base); increase only if natural terrain variation causes false positives.
When conservative_surface_heightmap detects a modified column (deviation beyond tolerance), place a layer with a fixed value instead of skipping entirely.
Layer value (1-8) to place when the surface is above RTF's expected base (terrain raised by structure), set to 0 to skip.
Layer value (1-8) to place when the surface is below RTF's expected base (terrain lowered by structure), set to 0 to skip.
config.aronalayersgen.option.structure_s: Skip layer placement where a structure elevated terrain above the RTF noise-derived surface Y. Only effective with injection_mode=POST_FEATURES and RTF active.
config.aronalayersgen.option.structure_r: When structure_skip_elevated=true and the elevation is exactly 1 block: replace the raised surface block with the correct layer instead of skipping.
When structure_replace_elevated=true: also apply replacement for elevations greater than 1 block (up to structure_replace_elevated_high_max).
Maximum elevation delta (blocks above natural surface) to apply high-elevation replacement. Positions elevated more than this are skipped.
config.aronalayersgen.option.structure_s: When structure_skip_elevated=true: after detecting an elevated position, also remove layer blocks within structure_skip_extra_cleanup_distance blocks of that position.
Chebyshev radius (blocks) around each elevated position to scan for layer blocks to remove.
config.aronalayersgen.option.dh_layer_ro: Distant Horizons only. DH stores LODs in whole blocks and draws every layer as a full block, so distant terrain stands a block too high wherever there are layers. With this on, layers are shown rounded: dh_layer_rounding_threshold layers or more as their full block, fewer as nothing (water if waterlogged).
Layer count (1-8) from which a layer shows as a full block in Distant Horizons LODs.
config.aronalayersgen.option.dh_exact_la: Distant Horizons only. Draw layers in LODs at their exact height (eighths of a block) instead of rounding them. Reaches into DH's internals, so it only switches on for the DH versions it was checked against (3.3.2 to 3.3.4); any other version uses the rounding above. Also patches DH's terrain shader and Iris's DH shader.

Distant Horizons only, with dh_exact_layers. Stores the eighths of a block in the lowest bits of the LOD colours instead of in DH's height fields, so exact heights also work in dimensions taller than 512 blocks (up to DH's own 4096 limit). Colours shift by at most 3/255. Only changes how LODs are drawn, never DH's saved data.
config.aronalayersgen.option.debug_loggi: Master switch for debug logging. The per-category switches only take effect while this is on.
